clue.text: Destroy resistance, mean, without hesitation

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: something done without a thing leaves it out, so the hesitation sound is dropped from the word for mean

parts.note: the mean of a set of numbers is its average
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A battle order: crush the resistance fighters, and be merciless about it, with no second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean looks like cruel in the surface, but it is the arithmetic average; hesitation is the filler sound a speaker makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravage a place is to lay it waste, a close synonym for wrecking it completely.

clue.text: Press one in trouble to give answer

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disarray, so these are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lean on someone who is already in difficulty to force a reply out of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply, which is what the noun answer means here.

clue.text: Legal volume with article on cover

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for volume
a is the indefinite article
a lid covers a pot or box

explanation.surface: A law book whose jacket carries a printed article.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, A sits on LID, after the V.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valid is legally sound and binding, as a valid contract or passport is.

clue.text: Fruit in odd parts of garden with promise

indicators.note: the odd parts are the first, third and fifth letters of the next word

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word
to engage oneself is to pledge or promise

explanation.surface: A fruit tree in an unusual corner of a garden that looks promising.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengage is a green-skinned variety of plum, a fruit grown in orchards and gardens.

clue.text: Bully in cast looking menacing

indicators.note: one word goes in another, so it sits inside the word for cast

parts.note: to cast a stone is to sling it
to cow someone is to bully them into submission

explanation.surface: A thuggish character among a play's cast, glowering at the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Bully and cast both read as nouns from the theatre, but each is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowling means frowning angrily, so a scowling face is one that looks threatening.

clue.text: Thousand, enthralled by broadcast clip, hear rare saxophonist

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so this letter is held inside the jumbled letters
to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the following letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
K is short for kilo, a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand listeners, spellbound by a radio clip, get to hear a rarely played sax recording.
explanation.walkthrough: The thousand is held inside the jumbled letters, near the end of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Parker, nicknamed Bird, was the American jazz alto saxophonist who pioneered bebop.

clue.text: Tolerate sport

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put up with or accept
second meaning: to have on, as in sporting a hat

explanation.walkthrough: Sport reads as a noun, a game, but here it is the verb meaning to have on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear as a verb means both to put up with something and to show off clothing on the body.

clue.text: Idyll's beginning thus with language about love and loneliness

indicators.note: one word is placed around another, so the language goes round the love
the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter
so means thus, in this way
the language of ancient Rome
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The start of a pastoral idyll, written in a language of love and solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero, as in a tennis score, and zero is written as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is the state of being cut off and alone, and so it means loneliness.

clue.text: Grand view around south over river in spring

parts.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: the word for view goes around the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to eye something is to view it
S is the compass abbreviation
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A grand view of the river from the south bank in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside EYE between its Y and second E; in a down clue that sits over R.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that shoots water and steam into the air, as at Yellowstone.

clue.text: Legend, about pixie and old partner with proposal and answer, easily understood

indicators.note: the word for legend goes about, that is around, the run of pieces that follows

parts.note: a legend is a traditional story
a pixie is a kind of elf
an ex is a former partner
a plan is a proposal
A is short for answer

explanation.surface: A folk tale about a pixie and a former lover, a marriage proposal and a reply, that needs no explaining.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first word wraps round all the rest; every other piece runs in clue order inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something self-explanatory needs no further explanation, so it is easily understood without help.

clue.text: Private investigation initially links big names

parts.note: private matters are personal ones

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: its first letter
ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: A private detective's inquiry turns up connections to famous people.
explanation.walkthrough: Private investigation suggests PI, but the two words are split: one a synonym, one a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Personalities are celebrities, famous people, just as big names are in showbusiness.

clue.text: Noise with hectic air in airport as a rule

indicators.note: the preceding pieces go in, that is inside, the airport's name

parts.note: Orly is one of the main airports serving Paris
a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: something hectic is frantic and disordered, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The racket and frantic atmosphere at an airport are what you normally get.
explanation.walkthrough: Orly is a Paris airport, a regular in crosswords alongside Heathrow's LHR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinarily means usually or normally, which is what the phrase as a rule means.

clue.text: Appointment kept by lord at embassy

indicators.note: something kept by these words is held within them, spanning the gaps

parts.note: inside lorD AT Embassy

explanation.surface: A meeting arranged by a peer at a foreign embassy.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is a fixed appointment, whether romantic or a set meeting time.

clue.text: Tone of old photographs, religious in the main?

indicators.note: one word goes in another, placed inside the word for the main

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open ocean
pi is slang for pious, religious

explanation.surface: A question whether the brown tint of antique photos is mainly religious in character.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for religious; the main is the sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the reddish-brown colour of early photographic prints, originally from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Stop enclosing area on large common

indicators.note: the word for stop encloses, that is surrounds, the letters that follow

parts.note: to prevent something is to stop it
A is the abbreviation for area
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Fencing off a big patch of village common land to keep people out.
explanation.walkthrough: Common in the surface is a noun, open public land in a British village; as the definition it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Prevalent means widespread or frequently found, so it is a synonym of common.

clue.text: Rewarded too highly in past with power and support

parts.note: something over is past or finished
P is the physics symbol for power
aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Someone who once got paid too much for being powerful and backed by friends.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overpaid is to receive more wages than the work merits, a straightforward equivalent.

clue.text: Value plot prepared for field event

indicators.note: letters prepared are made up into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plot of land valued and made ready to host an athletics competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole vault is an athletics jump over a high bar, one of the field events.

clue.text: Is emperor loudly upset over chapter of scientific evidence?

indicators.note: things upset are knocked out of order, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
Nero was a Roman emperor
f, forte, is the musical direction to play loudly
C is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: A question whether an emperor is noisily distressed over a chapter of lab findings.
explanation.walkthrough: Loudly looks like an adverb on the emperor's upset, but it supplies F, the music symbol for forte.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic describes science applied to criminal investigation, as in forensic evidence presented in court.

clue.text: Strange dream about time required to make sugar

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes about, that is around, the word for time
something strange is out of the usual shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A weird dream about the time needed to make sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the dream is jumbled; the period of time drops in whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a light brown cane sugar with large crystals, named after a region of Guyana.

clue.text: Learner at home with good old jargon

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate
someone at home is in
G is the abbreviation for good
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A student at home with an old textbook, picking up the technical vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: A British learner driver displays an L plate, so L means learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for specialist language or a foreign tongue, just as jargon is.

clue.text: A soldier in trouble for slow movement

indicators.note: the first pieces go in, placed inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
taken as written
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is in trouble for marching too slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Movement is not marching but a section of a symphony or sonata.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a slow section of a piece of music, played at a leisurely tempo.

clue.text: Diamonds are awfully expensive

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the word before is mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plain remark that diamonds cost a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Awfully reads as an intensifier for expensive, but it scrambles the word are.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage dear means costly, as in prices are dear this year.

clue.text: Music in stream's electronic, not adventurous

indicators.note: the style of music goes in, placed inside the word for stream

parts.note: a river is a stream, plus the S of the possessive
ska is a Jamaican music style
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A stream of music turns out to be electronic and rather unadventurous.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S of stream's is kept as a letter of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone risk-averse avoids taking chances, so they are cautious rather than daring.

clue.text: Pastoral artist restricted by endless regulation

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in, so the artist sits inside the trimmed word
with no end, the last letter of the word for regulation is dropped

parts.note: a rule is a regulation
RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A painter of country scenes hemmed in by never-ending rules.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy, London's leading art institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes the countryside and country life, so it is a synonym of rural.

clue.text: Conflict with spymaster getting heated

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A feud with the spy chief starts to boil over.
explanation.walkthrough: M is James Bond's boss, head of Britain's secret intelligence service in Ian Fleming's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm describes something moderately hot, so it can stand for heated.

clue.text: Regiment arranged rig used at sea

indicators.note: someone at sea is confused and lost, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military unit set up a rig to use out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Arranged looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; the signal is at sea. The Grenadier Guards are a senior British Army infantry regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grenadier Guards are a foot guards regiment of the British Army, famous for ceremonial duty.

clue.text: Work, mostly cautious, by saint, hopeful one

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for cautious is dropped

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a timid person is cautious and shy
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A rather cautious piece of work by a holy figure, a hopeful soul.
explanation.definitionFit: An optimist is a person who expects the best, so they are a hopeful one.

clue.text: Sloping island, one covered with powder

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

indicators.note: something covered with a substance is enclosed by it, so it sits inside the word for powder

parts.note: talc is a fine powder
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tilted island, with one part dusted in powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type is the slanted style of lettering, so it describes script that slopes.
